MECHANISM CLASS: Passivation/Inhibitor Chemistry Dosing

NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION)
This intervention proposes a schedule-driven dosing of a commercial molybdenum-oxide passivation inhibitor into the absorber loop via two standard peristaltic pumps. Standard practice maintains static alloy passivity; this mitigation actively replenishes the passive layer chemistry by dosing a standard catalog inhibitor at a controlled interval. The adjacent technique is standard industrial "chemical injection for corrosion inhibition." This is a genuine departure because it uses a specific *schedule* (dosing at low-temperature setpoints) to exploit the thermodynamic stability of the molybdate passive film, rather than just maintaining generic inhibitor levels. The mechanism attacks the failure's driving physics by raising the electrochemical potential for pitting, thereby reducing the pitting potential ($E_{pit}$).

PHYSICS CHECK
Governing relation: Pitting corrosion rate $i_p$ is governed by the transpassive current density $i_{trans}$ relative to the pitting potential $E_{pit}$. Adding molybdate ($MoO_4^{2-}$) increases $E_{pit}$, shifting the threshold for localized attack to higher, less attainable potentials.
Magnitude verification: Typical molybdate dosing (50–100 ppm) shifts $E_{pit}$ by 200–400 mV in chloride-bearing nitric acid systems, raising the overpotential margin against the $E_{corr}$ of 316L stainless steel under NOx/acid conditions.
DIRECTION-OF-EFFECT: driving variable = Pitting Potential ($E_{pit}$); the mechanism moves it UP by 200–400 mV via molybdate complexation on the passive film surface; this REDUCES the pitting corrosion rate by moving the system's operating potential away from the pitting threshold.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL
1. **Inhibitant Supply**: Commercial Molybdenum Oxide (MoO3) or Sodium Molybdate aqueous solution, standard industrial grade, stock SKU (e.g., Na2MoO4·2H2O 99% purity, commercial chemical class). (b)
   *Attachment: Installed into a standard HDPE day tank mounted on existing structural steel.*
   *Parameter: 2% w/v aqueous solution.*
2. **Dosing Hardware**: Two standard peristaltic dosing pumps, rated for chemical compatibility with nitric acid and inhibitors (e.g., PTFE-lined or PVDF diaphragm peristaltic, stock industrial grade), connected to existing process injection points. (b)
   *Attachment: Suction and discharge sides of the absorber loop, using existing 1/2" or 3/4" injection ports (standard process fittings).*
   *Parameter: 100–500 mL/hr each, scheduled.*
3. **Control Schedule**: Use existing DCS/PLC (stated infrastructure) to trigger dosing at 40°C setpoint. No new sensors. (c)
   *Parameter: Dose 500 mL of 2% molybdate every 4 hours when loop temperature < 40°C.*

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)
*Standard Practice Bill:* Passivity maintenance relies on alloy selection (no hardware) or generic inhibitor dosing (2 pumps, 1 tank, standard PLC).
*Your Bill:* Adds 2 standard peristaltic pumps (b), 1 standard HDPE tank (b), and a PLC schedule (c).
*Comparison:* No physical modification to the absorber (zero machining). No new sensors. No custom coating. No exotic materials.
*Operational Loss:* Zero throughput loss (dosing is open-loop volume, not flow restriction). Energy cost: ~2 kW for two pumps (negligible vs. absorber duty).
*Conclusion:* Same-or-lower burden class. Hardware is catalog-standard. No development. No custom calibration.

EXECUTABLE TEST
Protocol: Run two parallel absorber loops (or one loop A/B over 1 month).
*   Loop A: Control (no dosing).
*   Loop B: Dosing with 2% molybdate, 500 mL every 4 hours.
Instrument: Standard portable pH/conductivity meter (existing plant tool) and periodic metallographic sampling of standard witness coupons (commercial stock).
Pass/Fail Threshold: In Loop B, $E_{corr}$ measured by a commercial standard potential meter (procurable, standard class) must remain > 150 mV below $E_{pit}$ (determined by ASTM C876 polarization curve on witness coupons). No pitting visible on coupons after 30 days.
Kill Criterion: If Loop B shows pitting after 14 days, the inhibitor schedule is insufficient; increase dose or add chloride scavenger.
Duration: 30 days.
Falsifier validates EFFECTIVENESS: Corrosion rate (mmpy) on witness coupons drops by > 80% in Loop B vs. A.

CONSTRAINT BIND / RISK
*Permitted Set:* The constraint allows "passivation/inhibitor chemistry dosing." This mechanism is *exactly* that class.
*Exclusions:* No absorber redesign. No modification to stated device parts. The dosing pumps are added on the *surrounding system* (suction/discharge lines) and do not modify the absorber shell.
*Input Availability:* Requires existing DCS for scheduling. Requires standard conductivity/pH if used for control (but the schedule can be open-loop time-based, avoiding new instrumentation).
*Cost Pricing:* Dosing cost ~ $50/week for molybdate. Pump maintenance ~ $200/year. Net positive vs. absorber replacement (~ $200k).

UNPRICED_DUTY_CYCLE: the bill modulates a duty cycle or schedule but prices no operational cost (throughput/energy/availability, quantified or bounded) — the OPERATIONAL COST line is mandatory
